raw_case_text: A 29-year-old female patient, referred from general medicine department was presented with asymptomatic purplish and black colored skin lesions over the face (around lips) and extremities since past 15 days. Patient was a known and treated case of pulmonary tuberculosis and had taken complete anti-tubercular treatment 2 years back. Three months back, before the development of skin lesions, patient came to our hospital with complains of continuous cough and heaviness in chest. 2 D echo was carried out, which showed blocking in left pulmonary artery due to thrombus with right ventricular enlargement. Patient was put-on oral Warfarin 2.5 mg once daily to dissolve the thrombus. At that time her sputum was negative for acid fast bacilli (AFB). Two and half months later the patient came back with worsening of her chest complaints and on investigation she was found to have reactivation of pulmonary tuberculosis (sputum positive for AFB). She also had the above mentioned skin lesions for which she was referred to skin out patient department (OPD). General examination revealed her poor general condition with multiple purple to black ecchymotic patches around mouth, upper, and lower extremities [Figures 1 and 2]. Skin over right knee revealed black eschar surrounded by ecchymotic patch and erythema [Figure 3]. She also had resolving grouped vesicular lesions involving right L3, 4 dermatome, and clinically, suggestive of Herpes zoster. Routine investigations were within normal limits. Prothrombin time international normalized ratio (PTINR) of patient was carried out, which initially was not recordable as it was very high. We advised enzyme linked immune sorbent assay (ELISA) for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) antibodies taking in to consideration her reactivation of pulmonary tuberculosis, drug reaction, and herpes zoster. ELISA for HIV antibodies was reactive. Then the patient was admitted in medicine ward. Oral Warfarin was stopped and she was given two units of FFP on two alternate days. After giving one FFP, PTINR came down to 4 min, however, the patient died on the 4th day of admission.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 29-year-old female presenting with asymptomatic purplish-black cutaneous ecchymoses over the face and extremities for 15 days, in conjunction with worsening cough and chest heaviness.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed continuous cough and chest heaviness 3 months prior and was diagnosed with a left pulmonary artery thrombosis and right ventricular enlargement, for which oral warfarin was prescribed. Sputum AFB was negative at that time. Two and a half months later, she returned with worsening respiratory complaints, reactivation of pulmonary tuberculosis (sputum AFB positive), and newly erupted asymptomatic purple-to-black ecchymotic patches over her perioral area and extremities of 15 days' duration.
subjective.past_medical_history: Pulmonary tuberculosis treated with full course of anti-tubercular therapy completed 2 years prior. Left pulmonary artery thrombus with right ventricular enlargement diagnosed 3 months prior.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for continuous cough, chest heaviness, purpuric skin lesions, and resolving localized dermatomal rash; negative for fever, hemoptysis, or spontaneous mucosal hemorrhage. Home medications: oral warfarin 2.5 mg once daily. Allergies: unmentioned.

objective.physical_examination: General: poor general condition. Dermatologic: multiple purple-to-black ecchymotic patches around the mouth (perioral) and across upper and lower extremities; skin over the right knee demonstrated a necrotic black eschar surrounded by an ecchymotic patch and erythema; resolving grouped vesicular lesions along the right L3-L4 dermatome consistent with herpes zoster. Systemic examination: chest heaviness; other systemic findings unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Baseline routine investigations: within normal limits. Coagulation profile: prothrombin time international normalized ratio (PT/INR) markedly elevated and initially unrecordable (supratherapeutic), decreasing to 4 after fresh frozen plasma transfusion. Baseline sputum acid-fast bacilli (AFB) smear: positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
objective.advanced_workup: Transthoracic 2D echocardiography: left pulmonary artery thrombosis causing vascular obstruction, with right ventricular enlargement.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Severe warfarin-induced skin necrosis / coumarin necrosis with supratherapeutic coagulopathy, multi-dermatomal herpes zoster (VZV reactivation), and reactivated pulmonary tuberculosis, in newly diagnosed advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection. HIV confirmed by reactive ELISA for HIV antibodies. Tuberculosis confirmed by positive sputum acid-fast bacilli smear. Management & Outcome: Oral warfarin was immediately discontinued, and patient was admitted to the medical ward and administered 2 units of fresh frozen plasma (FFP) on alternate days. PT/INR improved to 4, but the patient experienced rapid clinical decline and succumbed on the 4th hospital day.
